web_evidence.title: With a Little Help From Her Friends
web_evidence.note: In an author interview, Patchett says she chose Lara's point of view and explicitly explains that she did not want another male first-person narrator after The Dutch House; the discussion treats Lara as narrator throughout the novel.

web_evidence.title: A review of Tom Lake by Ann Patchett
web_evidence.note: The review explicitly identifies Lara as the first-person narrator and explains that readers receive both her thoughts and the story she tells her daughters.

web_evidence.title: Tom Lake — Tamara Agha-Jaffar
web_evidence.note: The review describes two interlocking past and present threads and states that both are carried by Lara's first-person narrative voice, ruling out a change of person between timelines.

web_evidence.title: Tom Lake by Ann Patchett: An engrossing, utterly convincing meditation on life
web_evidence.note: The review identifies Lara as the novel's narrator and describes her interior monologues and private disclosures beyond what she tells her daughters, corroborated by first-person passages.

person_note: The Goodreads passages repeatedly expose Lara as a participating I/we narrator in both the 2020 orchard frame and her retrospective account of acting and Tom Lake. Story-specific addresses to her daughters and generalized uses of you are local address or aphorism, not second-person base narration; third-person references to Lara's younger self and other characters likewise do not create a separate narrating strand. Patchett's interview and multiple explicit whole-book reviews corroborate Lara's first-person narration across the interwoven timelines. Confidence is medium because no accessible sustained authorized excerpt or scholarly whole-book analysis was found.
